ios.desc:
Dice Baseball is a fast, fun baseball game powered by dice, strategy, and surprise moments.

Instead of complicated controls, every at-bat is decided by a roll. Hit singles, doubles, triples, home runs, or get caught at the wall as the defense tries to steal the play back.

Choose from unique stadiums that actually change how the game plays. High-altitude fields mean more home runs. Fast turf creates extra-base hits. Defensive parks make every run harder to earn.

Play solo against the computer or pass the phone for local player-vs-player games. Customize inning length, mercy rules, and stadiums to make every game feel different.

Dice Baseball also includes a kid-friendly “7th Minute Stretch” that encourages players to take a short break, move around, and jump back into the game refreshed.

Originally created with real dice and napkins at restaurants, Dice Baseball turns waiting time into game time while helping kids practice math, logic, and decision-making.

Dice Baseball is created by the team behind YouthBaseballTryouts.com, a platform dedicated to helping players and families find youth baseball opportunities across the country.

Baseball should always be fun, whether you are on the field, at a tryout, or rolling dice together at the table.

show_hn.title: Show HN: A dice baseball game I built with my second grader over winter break

quotes.text:
Over winter break, instead of the usual “kids playing in the snow” thing, we ended up doing something a little different. Mostly because it was abnormally warm, and partly because my kid had other ideas.

We built a small iPhone game together.

My son is a second grader and loves baseball. For years, our family has played a simple dice-based baseball game at restaurants while waiting for food. No screens. Just dice, rules scribbled on napkins, and a lot of arguing over whether something was a double or a ground out. It’s been one of those low-tech things that quietly stuck.

On the first night of winter break, he asked if we could turn it into an actual game.

So we did.

We spent the week breaking down how baseball works, how turns and randomness feel fair, and how games should be quick and fun. I introduced him to basic iPhone development concepts, UI thinking, and how we can use AI as a helper. Not to do the work for us, but to brainstorm, prototype, and iterate faster.

He was immediately hooked.

One of my favorite moments: he came up with a “7th minute stretch” idea. If a game session goes long enough, the app pauses and encourages you to get off the phone for 30 seconds. Do jumping jacks, grab water, stretch, whatever. It’s intentionally anti-doomscrolling, and very much his idea.

The result is Dice Baseball. A simple, fast, family-friendly dice baseball game for iPhone. No accounts. No ads. No paid features. There’s an optional tip jar if someone wants to support …
